title: Progressive waves; Stationary waves and harmonics
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W10-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; W01-uk1#t3 term and clue written for the game; W01-uk1#t1 term and clue written for the game; W10-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: W01-uk1#N.3, W10-1#N.4a, W01-uk1#N.5, W10-1#N.10, W01-uk1#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Node
items.clue: Point where the amplitude is zero at all times; the next one is λ/2 away.

items.label: In phase
items.clue: Relation between points one wavelength apart, which move exactly together.

items.label: Phase difference
items.clue: Angle equal to 2π times separation over λ; 90° for points a quarter of a cycle apart.

items.label: Reflection
items.clue: Bouncing back from a fixed end or pipe end, which supplies the partner moving the opposite way.

questions.stem: Two points on a progressive wave of wavelength 1.2 m are 0.40 m apart along the direction of travel. What is the phase difference between their oscillations?
questions.explanation: Right. Δx/λ = 0.40/1.2 = ⅓ cycle, and ⅓ × 2π = 2π/3 rad (120°).

questions.stem: A string fixed at both ends vibrates in a standing wave. Its nodes are at x = 0, 0.40 m, 0.80 m and 1.20 m, measured from one end. Points P, Q and R on the string are at x = 0.10 m, 0.20 m and 0.70 m. Which statement about the oscillations of P, Q and R is correct?

options.text: P and Q oscillate π/4 rad out of phase, being λ/8 apart.
P and Q oscillate in phase, with amplitudes equal to each other.
P and R oscillate in antiphase, with equal amplitudes.
P and R oscillate in phase, with equal amplitudes.

questions.stem: Two displacement–time graphs, P and Q, show the oscillations of two points on a wave. Both have a period of 6.0 ms. Each crest of Q comes 1.0 ms after the matching crest of P. What is the phase difference between P and Q?

A string fixed at both ends vibrates in its first harmonic. The tension in the string is then increased to four times its original value, with the length and the string unchanged. By what factor does the frequency of the first harmonic change?

A loudspeaker emits a steady 500 Hz note. Two microphones are placed on a straight line from the loudspeaker, 0.17 m apart. The speed of sound is 340 m s⁻¹. How do the oscillations detected by the two microphones compare?

options.text: They are in antiphase, π rad apart.
They are a quarter of a cycle, π/2 rad, apart.
They are in phase, as the note has one frequency.
They are an eighth of a cycle, π/4 rad, apart.
